priority queue: properly sync the `waiter` manipulation

As described in https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/controller-runtime/issues/3363,
there are some circumstances under which `GetWithPriority`
is not returning the correct/expected element.

This can happen when a `GetWithPriority` is executed
and the `Ascend` of the queue is not completed yet,
causing not all the items of the BTree to evaluate
the same w.waiters.Load() value.

Adding a lock to manipulate the waiters will solve the issue.
Since the lock is required, there is no need to use an
atomic.Int64 anymore.

envtest: respect pre-configured binary paths in ControlPlane

This commit fixes an issue where Environment.Start() would ignore
pre-configured binary paths (APIServer.Path, Etcd.Path, KubectlPath)
set in ControlPlane when DownloadBinaryAssets is false.

Changes:
- Extract path configuration logic into configureBinaryPaths() method
  for better testability and separation of concerns
- Only auto-configure binary paths when they are empty (not pre-set)
- When DownloadBinaryAssets is true, downloaded paths are still used
  (preserving existing behavior)
- Update ControlPlane field documentation to clarify path behavior
- Add tests in envtest_test.go to verify path handling logic

Deflake should execute the Warmup function when Warmup group is started

The test is flaky as visible in both PRs and the periodic. The reason is
that it calls Start() which asynchronously starts a runnable and expects
said runnable to finish immediately after which may or may not work out
depending on how busy the box the test is run on is.

Use `synctest` instead, as that allows us to explicitly block until all
asynchronous operations that can finish are finished.

:seedling: Priorityqueue: Use separate b-trees for ready and non-ready items

This change refactors the priorityqueue to use distinct b-trees for
ready and non-ready items. This simplifies the code, because the two of
them effectively have different sorting requirements. We made this work
using one b-tree sorted by priority first and readyAt second and then
iterating through all priorities high to low until we find a ready item.
While correct, this is difficult to reason about.

The other issue is that currently, there is no explicit transition step
from non-ready to ready. As a result, we always had to iterate over all
items in case one got ready to then update metrics. With this change, we
instead have an explicit event when an item gets ready and we can then
update metrics for just this item and do not have to iterate over
everything.

them effectively have different sorting requirements. We made this work
using one b-tree sorted by priority first and readyAt second and then

from non-ready to ready. As a result, we always had to iterate over all
items in case one got ready to then update metrics. With this change, we
instead have an explicit event when an item gets ready and we can then
update metrics for just this item and do not have to iterate over

* Fix IndexField blocking until informer is synced

IndexField() was blocking until the informer cache synced, causing
unnecessary delays during controller startup. This happens because
GetInformer() defaults to blockUntilSync=true.

However, adding an index doesn't require the informer to be synced -
the underlying client-go threadSafeStore.AddIndexers doesn't depend
on sync state. Only List operations with field selectors need the
cache to be synced.

This test verifies that IndexField returns immediately when called
before the informer cache is synced, using BlockUntilSynced(false).

context. If IndexField blocks waiting for sync, it will timeout with
a clear error message.

:bug: ensure envtest stops the whole process group

A previous pull request attempted to prevent envtest from leaking
orphaned etcd / kube-apiserver etc. processes by adding a SysProcAttr of
`Setpgid: true`. However, it made a few mistakes:

- It incorrectly described the change as causing the process to "inherit
  the parent's process group id", which is the opposite of what it does.
  In fact it causes a brand new process group to be created for the child
  process, which is the actual behaviour we want, so correct the comment.
- Whilst it added a new process group, it didn't update the signalling
  to send SIGTERM (and eventually SIGKILL) to the process group (by
  using a `-` prefix) and was still just sending the signal to the process
  itself.
- It didn't add a unittest to assert on the desired behaviour before and
  after the changes.

This PR should hopefully fix all of those problems and result in fewer
process leaks.

🐛 Fix PriorityQueue deadlock on shutdown (#3540)

* 🐛 Fix PriorityQueue deadlock on shutdown

handleReadyItems hands a ready item to a waiting consumer with an
unbuffered send on w.get while holding w.lock. If ShutDown shuts the
w.done channel first, the parked GetWithPriority consumer can return
through <-w.done instead of receiving, so the send blocks forever and the
whole queue deadlocks (every later GetWithPriority and handleAddBuffer
blocks on w.lock).

Wrap the send in a select that also watches w.done so it is cancelled on
shutdown. Add a regression test that runs the reporter's add/get loop and
fails if workers stay blocked after ShutDown.

:bug: fake: fix AddIndex panic when client is wrapped with an interceptor

Motivation:
fake.AddIndex type-asserted the passed client.Client directly to
*fakeClient. When a fake client is built with
ClientBuilder.WithInterceptorFuncs(...), Build() wraps the *fakeClient
in an interceptor value, so the assertion always failed and AddIndex
panicked with "AddIndex can only be used with a fake client", even
though a real fake client was underneath.

Approach:
Add an Unwrap() client.WithWatch method to the interceptor type
(pkg/client/interceptor/intercept.go), mirroring the standard Go
"Unwrap" convention. AddIndex now uses a small unwrapFakeClient helper
that loops through any client implementing that method to find the
underlying *fakeClient, instead of relying on a single type assertion.

Validation:
- go build ./... succeeds.
- go test ./pkg/client/fake/... ./pkg/client/interceptor/... passes.
- Added a Ginkgo test reproducing the issue: building a client via
  NewClientBuilder().WithInterceptorFuncs(interceptor.Funcs{}).Build()
  and calling AddIndex on it. Verified this test panics with "AddIndex
  can only be used with a fake client" against the pre-fix code and
  passes against the fix (failing-then-passing check).
- go vet and golangci-lint run on the changed packages report no
  issues.
- No behavior change for callers that pass a bare *fakeClient.

[release-0.25] 🐛 client: fix subresource create RV parse error under read-your-writes consistency (#3596)

* 🐛 client: fix subresource create RV parse error under read-your-writes consistency

Motivation:

With client.Options.Cache.EnableReadYourWritesConsistency enabled, a
subresource Create whose response is not the target object itself -
for example evicting a Pod via
c.SubResource("eviction").Create(ctx, pod, &policyv1.Eviction{...}) -
fails with "failed to parse resource version : strconv.ParseInt:
parsing \"\": invalid syntax", even though the request is executed by
the API server (the Pod is actually evicted).

Approach:

consistentClient.writeAndRecordRV reads the resource version to wait
for from the object passed as its first argument after the write
completes. For a normal Create/Update/Patch/Apply that object is the
one the server's response is decoded into, so that is correct. For a
SubResource Create, the target object (e.g. the Pod) and the response
object (e.g. the Eviction) are different arguments, and the server's
response is decoded into the latter, not the former
(typedClient.CreateSubResource decodes .Into(subResourceObj)). Reusing
writeAndRecordRV therefore read the resource version off an object the
write never touched, which is empty whenever the caller didn't already
have it at hand (as in the eviction example above), causing the
parse error.

Adds consistentClient.writeSubResourceAndRecordRV, used only by
consistentSubResourceClient.Create, which keeps using the target
object for the write-barrier/consistency-handler bookkeeping but reads
the resource version from the actual response object instead. Some
subresource-create responses, notably Eviction and Binding, are a bare
Status on success and carry no resource version at all; mirroring how
Delete already tolerates a response with no resource version, this
treats that as "nothing to wait for" rather than an error - matching
the behavior of DisableReadYourWritesConsistency, which is what the
issue asks for. This does not make read-your-writes consistency
actually wait for the effect of such subresource creates (e.g. a
subsequent Get for the evicted Pod through the same client is not
guaranteed to reflect the eviction); it only stops those calls from
failing with an unrelated parse error. This limitation is called out
in the new method's doc comment.

Validation:

go build ./... and go vet ./pkg/client/... pass.

Added TestConsistentFakeClientSubResourceCreateWithoutResponseResourceVersion
in pkg/client/consistency_fake_test.go, which creates a Pod and calls
SubResource("eviction").Create with a Pod argument that only has
Namespace/Name set (no resource version, matching how eviction callers
typically use it) and expects it to succeed. Confirmed this test fails
on the pre-fix code with the exact reported error
(failed to parse resource version : strconv.ParseInt: parsing "":
invalid syntax) and passes after the fix.

go test ./pkg/client/... passes, including the envtest-backed suites
in pkg/client and pkg/client/apiutil, run with KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS
pointed at kubebuilder-assets 1.37.0 via setup-envtest.

Additionally ran the issue's own minimal reproduction (a Pod eviction
against a real envtest 1.37.0 apiserver, with and without
DisableReadYourWritesConsistency) from a scratch package inside this
module; both subtests pass with a nil error, matching the issue's
expected behavior.

golangci-lint run ./pkg/client/... (v2.12.2; CI pins v2.13.1) reports
no findings in the changed files.
